note: Trading tens and ones blueprint (OLL decision 0023, need K2N-23 of the frozen K-12 component map), 2026-11-22. One row per idea, from the Common Core standards: 1.NBT.B.2.a and c, 1.NBT.A.1 (a collection up to 120 written as a numeral), 2.NBT.A.1.a and b, 2.NBT.A.3. Each row's teacher picture says what a good teacher draws, written without reference to any card. Cases (development and scoring) are written from these rows, worded as learners ask. English only: the mat's own words (Make a ten, the refusals) are English. Never taken from the question set.

rows.teacher_picture: Loose unit cubes; ten of them gathered and bundled (or snapped into a rod) to make one ten; the rod is the same length as ten cubes in a row. States: the loose ones; ten gathered; one ten.
Ten-rods only, for example 6 rods named sixty: six tens and zero ones; sometimes built from loose ones bundled ten at a time until none are left over.

rows.idea: A collection counted by bundling tens, up to 120
rows.teacher_picture: A pile of objects (straws, sticks, cubes) bundled into tens with a few left over; the bundles and the leftovers counted and the number written: 4 bundles and 7 left is 47. Past 100, ten bundles make a hundred: 11 bundles and 3 is 113.

rows.idea: Hundreds, tens and ones; 100 as ten tens; a place with zero
rows.teacher_picture: Flats, rods and unit cubes on a place-value mat; ten rods traded for one flat; a pile with too many ones or tens regrouped until each place has fewer than ten, then read: 706 is 7 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones.
A number shown with flats, rods and cubes and written by places: 345 = 300 + 40 + 5; each part is what that place is worth.
